products.name: InternLM (Shanghai AI Lab)
products.note: Chinese open-source LLM; academic research; cross-border data review advised

reading.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a government-affiliated research institution in China operating InternLM, an open-source large language model positioned for academic research across Chinese universities and scientific applications.

The laboratory's stated focus spans model capability, embodied robotics, and AI safety frameworks, with recent emphasis on science-oriented systems that integrate language models, specialist agents, and physical automation. This portfolio suggests a research strategy prioritizing broad capability development rather than any single domain constraint. The 2026 announcement of AI-for-science results and a scientific discovery platform indicates the institution is testing large models as infrastructure for experimental workflows, from hypothesis through validation.

What matters for AI infrastructure is that Shanghai AI Laboratory operates within China's university and research ecosystem, not as a commercial infrastructure builder or power provider. The laboratory contributes to model capability and research methodology but does not control the compute, buildings, or power grids that determine how quickly those capabilities can scale. It represents the downstream user of infrastructure, not the constraint that binds it.

The data does not cover the laboratory's budget, its access to compute hardware, or the power requirements of its training and inference systems. Without those facts, the connection between its research ambitions and the infrastructure constraints that may or may not enable them remains unmeasured.

profile_text.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a non-profit government laboratory whose website is shlab.org.cn. Its site describes it as recruiting young researchers worldwide in fields including artificial intelligence, large models, embodied intelligence, safe and trustworthy AI, AI for Science, basic platforms, the innovation chain, and management support, with the stated aim of working toward AGI. Since 2022 the lab says it has run a joint doctoral training program with more than ten universities, among them Peking University, Tsinghua University, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tongji University, the University of Science and Technology of China, and Zhejiang University.

The lab's tracked product is InternLM, listed as a Chinese open-source large language model used in academic research, with cross-border data review advised. Its site describes several further releases: an upgraded scientific discovery platform presented at the 2026 Pujiang Innovation Forum, with its full-stack services opened up, a physical world model named W0, and an embodied full-stack engine called Intern-Robotics. At the 2026 WAIC science frontier forum the lab says it released ten joint innovation results with universities, research institutes, and industry partners, covering life sciences, materials science, and deep space astronomy.

On technical direction, the site describes a general-specialized fusion system built in three layers, and quotes Professor Zhou Bowen arguing that scientific research is the next programming and that AI and science will form a dual-wheel drive. It also describes an AI-45 degree balance law for safety and performance, a causal path toward trustworthy AGI through alignment, intervention, and reflection stages, and risk management spanning evaluation, training, foundation, application, and verification. The site advertises a "North Star" talent program for global recruitment.
